compiled_state.author: Rebar Bot
compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem

`.github/workflows/prompt-eval.yml` runs its live tier on a weekly cron across every
dataset-bearing spec, bounded only by `REBAR_EVAL_MAX_CASES: "12"` per spec, and its own
comment records that no dollar ceiling exists in that lane: "Hard dollar caps live at the
provider dashboard (CI has none)."

Letting the criteria covered by this epic join that sweep would multiply its per-run call
count several-fold every week, in perpetuity, and would grow again with each criterion
added later. The cron is also the wrong instrument for these fixtures: they exist to catch a
criterion-rubric regression, and a rubric regression arrives with a commit rather than with
the passage of time.

## Approach

Execute a criterion's fixtures when that criterion's rubric changes.

The selection itself is a rebar operation, not a CI feature: a shared engine function maps a
changed-file set to the criterion ids whose rubric files appear in it, resolving each against
`criteria.effective_routing('.', gate_key='plan_review')` and its prompt id. The CLI exposes
it as `rebar criteria eval --changed-since <ref>`; any other surface calls the same function
rather than re-implementing the mapping, so the rule cannot drift between surfaces.

**Portability.** This capability must not depend on any one CI provider. The trigger is
operation-linked: a developer runs the command locally against any git range and gets the
same selection, and a project with no CI provider gets the same behavior from the same
command. The workflow job is a thin caller of that command, not the place the logic lives.
The command shells out to nothing POSIX-specific and takes its repository root from the
existing resolution path rather than assuming a `.rebar/` directory under the process's
working directory.

**CI trigger classification.** The new job is added to `prompt-eval.yml`, whose existing
`push` trigger carries `branches-ignore: ["feature/**", "main", "tickets"]` and a
`pull_request: {}` filter. Against this epic's work: the `pull_request` trigger is INCLUDED
(a rubric edit arrives on a pull request and is the case this job exists for); the `push`
trigger is INCLUDED for ordinary branches and EXCLUDED for `main`, `feature/**` and
`tickets`, which is correct because those lanes are the mirror, the replicated feature
namespace, and the event log respectively; the weekly `schedule` trigger is EXCLUDED for the
new job, which is the point of this child. No trigger is left NO_FILTER.

## Scope

The shared changed-rubric selection function, its CLI flag, and the workflow job that calls
it. The existing weekly live sweep keeps its current spec set.

## Non-goals

- Changing the weekly cron's behavior for the specs it already covers.
- Making the new job a required or blocking check; it stays non-blocking like the existing
  live tier.
- Any dollar-ceiling mechanism inside GitHub Actions.

## Compatibility and rollback

Purely additive: one new engine function, one new CLI flag, one new workflow job. The
offline tier, which is the only required check, and the existing weekly live tier are
untouched. Back-out is deleting the job and the flag; there is no persisted state and no
format change, so no expand-contract sequencing applies.

## Testing

A real CLI subprocess against temporary git repositories with seeded commits exercises the
selection across a rubric-touching range, a non-rubric range, and an unmappable rubric path;
the subprocess tier is required because the behavior includes argument parsing, git range
resolution and exit codes. A unit test covers the workflow's resolved spec list. The
repository's existing actionlint test node covers workflow validity.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A range touching `plan_review_T8.md` and `plan_review_G6.md` selects exactly the
      criterion ids `T8` and `G6`; verified by a `pytest` subprocess test asserting the
      printed selection against a seeded temporary repository.
- [ ] A range touching no rubric file selects nothing, exits `0`, and issues no model call;
      verified by the same subprocess test asserting an empty selection and `exit code` 0
      with no model configured.
- [ ] A rubric path matching no registry criterion is named on stderr rather than skipped
      silently; verified by `pytest` asserting the warning text for a seeded
      `plan_review_bogus.md`.
- [ ] The prompt ids covered by this epic are absent from the weekly sweep's resolved spec
      list; verified by `pytest` asserting the intersection is empty.
- [ ] The command produces a selection with no CI environment variables set; verified by a
      `pytest` subprocess test run with a cleared environment.
- [ ] The workflow file passes the repository's existing actionlint check; verified by
      `pytest` over that node.

## Definition of Done

`make lint`, `make typecheck` and `make test` pass; a rubric-touching range selects only the
affected criteria; a non-rubric range selects none.

## Budget

**Hard cap $25**, covering verification runs while developing this child. Steady-state cost
afterwards is zero unless a rubric changes, at which point one criterion runs.

file_impact.reason: Shared engine function mapping a changed-file set to the criterion ids whose rubric files it touches.
Expose the selection as `rebar criteria eval --changed-since <ref>`, calling the shared engine function rather than reimplementing the mapping.
Add the change-triggered job as a thin caller, and keep the new specs out of the weekly live sweep's resolved list.
Subprocess tests over seeded temporary git repositories for the selection, the empty case, the unmappable rubric path and the no-CI-environment case.

compiled_state.title: Run a criterion's fixtures when its rubric changes, keeping them off the weekly live sweep
